t: Lukouchiao incident.
Japanese attack Langfang with troops and planes.
Japanese detachment ambushed and attacked in the Kuang An Men, Peiping.
Mutiny of East Hopei Peace Preservation Corps and massacre of Japanese at Tungchow.
Pao An Tui at Tientsin attack Japanese who respond with heavy aerial bombing.
Japanese occupy Nankow Pass.
Kalgan occupied by Japanese.
Paotingfu and Tsangchow occupied.
Japanese cross Shantung border.
Kweihua occupied.
Japanese occupy Niangtzekwan Pass.
Occupation of Taiyuanfu completed by Japanese.
Destruction of Japanese cotton mills and other industrial plants at Tsingtao.
Japanese occupy Tsinanfu.
Outbreak of hostilities at Shanghai.

Chinese planes drop bombs in International Settlement, causing 729 deaths and wounding 861 between Cathay and Palace Hotels in Nanking Road, and killing 1,012 and wounding 1,007 at junction of Avenue Edward VII and Boulevard de Montigny.

Japanese troops force landing near Woosung. Chinese plane drops bombs in International Settlement: one (which did not explode) behind Hamilton House, and another on Sincere Co.'s Emporium, killing 215 and wounding 558 persons.
President Hoover bombed by Chinese planes outside Woosung.
British Ambassador shot and seriously wounded by machine-gunning from Japanese plane while motoring from Nanking to Shanghai.
Chinese withdraw from Shanghai Civic Centre and Far Eastern Race Course.
Japanese announce intention to bomb Nanking.
Four air-raids, in which 80 Japanese planes took part, on Nanking, which hereafter was bombed almost daily.
British soldier (Rifleman W. McGowan) killed outside Q. Post in Keswick Road, Shanghai, by machine-gunning from Japanese plane.
Chinese evacuate Chapei and Kiangwan (Shanghai), withdrawing south of Soochow Creek.
Three Ulster Riflemen mortally wounded by Japanese shell-fire near Jessfield Park, Shanghai.
Japanese force crossing of Soochow Creek, Shanghai.
Surprise Japanese landing near Chapoo.
Chinese withdraw from Hungjao area, Shanghai, beyond Lunghwa and Tsingpu.
Chinese resistance in Nantao, Shanghai, ends.
Kiating captured.
Quinsan falls.
Changshu and Kashing fall.
Japanese capture Soochow. Only 500 out of population of 200,000 remain in city.
Wusih captured.
6,000 Japanese troops parade through International Settlement from Brenan Road to Garden Bridge. Bomb outrage in which several Japanese soldiers and onlookers were wounded in Nanking Road.
U.S.S. Panay sunk by Japanese aerial bombing above Nanking. H.M.S. Ladybird badly damaged by Japanese shell-fire off Wuhu.
Nanking occupied by Japanese.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: A fire in a printing works at Nantao caused damage to the extent of some $30,000.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: A fire in a pharmacy in Yunnan Road, Central District, cost insurance companies $98,000.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: A waste cotton godown and factory in Chapei was gutted, the damage amounting to $130,000.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: An outbreak in one of Liddell's cotton godowns in Yangtszepoo caused a loss of some $25,000.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: A fire in a row of shops in Boulevard des Deux Republiques, French Concession, did damage to the extent of $40,000.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: One of the most disastrous cotton fires ever recorded in Shanghai occurred on July 8, when Godowns E5 and F6 of the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Co.'s Pootung Wharf were totally destroyed. The insurances in force amounted to over $2,000,000, and total losses have been paid under most of the policies concerned owing to the fact that, due to the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, it was not possible to recover and recondition the damaged cotton, from which at one time it was hoped for a 40 per cent salvage. The Chinese insurance companies carried the bulk of the insurance.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: A disastrous fire broke out in the Ting Kee Native Bank godown in the Northern District of Shanghai, when piece goods and other merchandise to the value of $1,084,300 were more or less totally destroyed, the loss being increased by the fact that salvage work was stopped by the fighting which broke out a few days later.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: The contents of godowns of the Tientsin Press Packing Co. in the British Concession at Tientsin were damaged to the extent of $75,000 by fires in January and February.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: A serious fire at the wood oil plant of the Arnhold Trading Co., Hankow, resulted in a loss of $206,000.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: A godown of the Mitsui Bussan Kaisha at Hankow was partly destroyed, with a loss of $55,000.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: There were several extensive fires in blocks of Chinese shops and dwellings in Hankow during April and May with a total loss of over $150,000.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: A fire in a hardware shop in the former British Concession at Hankow cost insurance companies $125,000.

a: Insurance in China — [Serious Fires in Shanghai and the Outports, 1937]
t: A paint and varnish factory at Hankow was destroyed by fire, with a loss of $28,000.
